input.content: Pattern: an independently released client hard-requires a new response field (e.g. receipt/"applied" acknowledgement) that only a pending provider task will add, and the check is unconditional, not behind the feature flag. Against the released provider the side effect still happens (the settings get stored), but the client raises, so every ordinary operation reports failure even with the feature disabled. Detect it by running the client against the release-tag provider source (git show <tag>:path), not against a test fake shaped like the new protocol. Fix: gate the new requirement on the feature flag or on capability negotiation, keep the legacy success path, and add a test using the legacy response shape.
